newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan long-term prime likely to be cut to 2.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Japan long-term prime likely to be cut to 2.7 pct.

text.p: Japan's long-term prime rate is likely to be cut by 0.3 percentage point to 2.7 percent, bond traders said on Monday.
A spokeswoman for the Industrial Bank of Japan said the bank would announce a change in its long-term prime rate sometime in the afternoon.
The prime rate, that at which long-term credit banks lend to their most creditworthy customers, has been set at 3.0 percent since September.
The other two long-term credit banks, the Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan Ltd (LTCB) and Nippon Credit Bank Ltd (NCB), are expected to follow suit on Tuesday.
The IBJ customarily sets its long-term prime rate 0.9 percentage point above that of its debenture coupon rate and the other two banks adopt the same prime rate.
The yield of the latest IBJ debentures, issued in September with a 2.1 percent coupon, stood at around 1.8 percent on Monday, traders said.
